title: Derive component names from the artifact resource plus a capability suffix

facts.note: Planning task mentions naming or declaring components that handle artifacts.
Planner is authoring plans/wagons/features where components are declared.

values: component declaration or component URN added/renamed in a plan artifact
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer that extracts new/renamed component names and the artifact resource/type they handle.

values: component name stem not traceable to the handled artifact
facts.note: No implementation exists (implementation.type: none); a name/suffix checker would be new.
Planner audience; applies while planning, not while coding.

fires: Planner declares a new component that handles an event artifact and must choose its name.
Planner names a component from an artifact resource and type before the full artifact URN is finalised.
Planner writes a component URN for a component handling a state, data or config artifact.
Planner renames a component whose handled artifact resource is known.
doesNotFire: Naming the artifact itself (artifact naming pattern is a separate, prerequisite convention).
Planning work that declares no components (e.g. editing acceptance prose only).
Coder naming internal helpers, variables or test files that are not planned components.

given: A planned component handles an artifact whose resource (the part after the colon) and type are known, even if the full URN is not yet final.
when: The planner names the component or writes its component URN.
then: Name the component as the PascalCase artifact resource plus a capability suffix chosen by artifact type and the component's responsibility.
prefer: PascalCase the resource first (player-wallet→PlayerWallet), then append the suffix.
Suffix catalogs: events (past tense) Publisher/Emitter/Broadcaster; states (adjective) Tracker/Monitor/Manager; data (noun) Provider/Handler/Processor/Maker; configs Configurator/Builder/Initializer.

Source examples use an artifact-derived stem that qualifies or replaces the literal resource: match:started→MatchStartedPublisher, wallet:credited→WalletCreditedEmitter, timebank.remaining→TimebankTracker, session:active→SessionManager, match:config→MatchConfigurator, league:config→LeagueBuilder. The source does not reconcile these with the literal rule; keep any stem traceable to the artifact.

One artifact may fan out to several components across sides/layers; the source's worked example also uses responsibility suffixes outside the catalogs: ChoiceDisplay (presentation UI), ChoiceValidator (validation), ChoicePersister (persistence), alongside ChoiceMaker.
Let the name describe the CAPABILITY to handle the artifact.
avoid: A suffix unrelated to the artifact type.
Names not traceable to the handled artifact.
why: Mechanical derivation from the artifact resource keeps component names predictable and traceable to the artifact they handle, while the type-driven suffix encodes the component's capability.
evidence: For each planned component, the reviewer identifies the handled artifact, takes the resource after the colon, and confirms the name starts with its PascalCase form or an artifact-derived stem of the kind shown in the source examples.

The suffix is in the catalog for the artifact's type, or is one of the responsibility suffixes the source's worked example uses (Display for presentation, Validator for validation, Persister for persistence) for the matching responsibility; a suffix contradicting the artifact type fails.
The component name is PascalCase and is reused verbatim in the component URN (component:<wagon>:<feature>.<Name>.<side>.<layer>).
verifier_detail: Resource = substring of the artifact URN after the colon; for dotted URNs (e.g. aspect.resource) the source examples use the final segment as the resource.
PascalCase normalisation examples: choice→Choice, player-wallet→PlayerWallet, domain-impacts→DomainImpacts, remaining→Remaining.

Type classification heuristics: events = past-tense resources (started, closed, credited); states = adjective resources (remaining, active, current); data = noun resources (choice, identity, profile); configs = configuration resources (config, settings, agreement).
Suffix catalogs: events {Publisher, Emitter, Broadcaster}; states {Tracker, Monitor, Manager}; data {Provider, Handler, Processor, Maker}; configs {Configurator, Builder, Initializer}.

Source examples (event): match:started (resource started) → MatchStartedPublisher (component:resolve-dilemmas:make-choice.MatchStartedPublisher.backend.integration); wallet:credited (resource credited) → WalletCreditedEmitter (component:manage-wallets:credit-wallet.WalletCreditedEmitter.backend.integration).

Source examples (state): mechanic:timebank.remaining (resource remaining) → TimebankTracker (component:burn-timebank:track-timebank.TimebankTracker.backend.domain); session:active (resource active) → SessionManager (component:init-session:maintain-session.SessionManager.backend.application).

Source examples (data): mechanic:decision.choice (resource choice) → ChoiceMaker (component:resolve-dilemmas:make-choice.ChoiceMaker.backend.domain); player:identity (resource identity) → IdentityProvider (component:contextualize-identity:identify-player.IdentityProvider.backend.application).

Source examples (config): match:config (resource config) → MatchConfigurator (component:setup-match:configure-match.MatchConfigurator.backend.application); league:config (resource config) → LeagueBuilder (component:define-league:configure-league.LeagueBuilder.backend.application).
Summary examples: resource 'started' (event) → MatchStartedPublisher; resource 'remaining' (state) → TimebankTracker.

Worked fan-out example: artifact mechanic:decision.choice, wagon resolve-dilemmas, feature make-choice → ChoiceDisplay (component:resolve-dilemmas:make-choice.ChoiceDisplay.frontend.presentation; renders choice options to user; 'choice'→ChoiceDisplay, presentation UI), ChoiceValidator (component:resolve-dilemmas:make-choice.ChoiceValidator.frontend.application; validates user selection before submission; validation logic), ChoiceMaker (component:resolve-dilemmas:make-choice.ChoiceMaker.backend.domain; applies business rules to make the choice; core business logic), ChoicePersister (component:resolve-dilemmas:make-choice.ChoicePersister.backend.integration; persists choice to database; persistence).

Source ambiguity (also stated to planners in prefer[2]/prefer[3]): several examples use an artifact-derived stem instead of or in addition to the literal resource, and the worked example uses Display/Validator/Persister outside the catalogs. Detector: accept artifact-traceable stems; accept catalog suffixes for the artifact's type plus the source-shown responsibility suffixes for their matching responsibility; flag non-PascalCase names and suffixes contradicting the artifact type.
Counter-example: 'choiceHandler' (not PascalCase) or a suffix unrelated to the artifact type.

additions.text: Reviewer checks that the derived name is reused verbatim in the component URN (component:<wagon>:<feature>.<Name>.<side>.<layer>).
additions.justification: URN shape is generalised from the source example URNs so a reviewer has a concrete check; no new obligation beyond the source's naming rule.

additions.text: Explicit note on source ambiguity (artifact-derived stems; out-of-catalog responsibility suffixes) and how a detector should tolerate it.
additions.justification: The source's own examples deviate from a literal reading of the statement; without this note a detector would reject the source's canonical examples. The same ambiguity is shown to planners in prefer[2]/prefer[3] so both audiences share one rule.
Required by the target schema; derived from the rule's scope (planner naming components from artifact resources).
Losslessness: the source's domain-qualified stem examples and out-of-catalog responsibility suffixes are decision-relevant for planners and must be author-facing.
